### R and R-Studio

[R](http://www.r-project.org) is a free open-source programming language that can be used for statistical analysis, data-simulation, graphing, and lots of other stuff. Another free program is [R-studio](http://www.rstudio.com), that provides a nice graphic interface for R. Download R first, then download R-studio. Both can run on PCs, Macs or Linux. Students will be learning R in the stats labs using the lab manual []().

### Climatology

1. [Ecological Climatology](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/ecological-climatology/D146443B007985BC366B2512345692C0?pageNum=1&searchWithinIds=D146443B007985BC366B2512345692C0&productType=BOOK_PART&searchWithinIds=D146443B007985BC366B2512345692C0&productType=BOOK_PART&sort=mtdMetadata.bookPartMeta._mtdPositionSortable%3Aasc&pageSize=30&template=cambridge-core%2Fbook%2Fcontents%2Flistings&ignoreExclusions=true) is great.
2. [Terrestrial Biosphere-Atmosphere Fluxes](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/terrestrial-biosphereatmosphere-fluxes/43C9DC719235C8832D6BD6D90B6EFA49) is great.
3. Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) [Crop evapotranspiration](https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm#Contents) website, it's worth checking out.
